extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists, literary students, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for writing and judging novels: how to shape subject, time, point of view, scene construction, character consistency, and authorial method so the work forms a coherent artistic 'picture'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of a distinctive imaginative world
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist may 'create a “world of their own”' (as Balzac, Stendhal, Maupassant do) or may look at the common world and make more of it by genius (as Tolstoy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the writer establishes a consistent, self-contained sense of place and social reality that feels original and convincing. Example/contrast: some writers invent a unique world; others intensify ordinary reality. Both are valid but must be cohesive and sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of space and daylight (spatial/temporal continuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuity of space and daylight is 'so necessary to the motive of the book' and must be rendered consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The physical and temporal continuity of scenes should support the book's motive; lapses or jarring breaks in spatial or daylight continuity weaken the sense of a lived world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of the passage of time (form of time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The movement of the wheel of time must be made perceptible; 'the form of time is to be represented, and that is something more than to represent its contents in their order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on mere chronological listing or announcements ('years have fled'); the book's lines and masses (its form and structure) should make time's passage felt. Consider techniques that show both incremental change and large arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing both continuous lapse and cyclical/generative sweep of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time has a double effect: 'its uninterrupted lapse, and the cycle of which the chosen stretch is a segment' — e.g., accumulation of years and the rise-and-fall curve of a generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent both the quotidian slipping of time (faces, gestures, texture of thought) and the larger generational arc so the reader perceives both everyday change and the grand sweep or cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters age and change while retaining sameness (consistency through growth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should 'grow older...with the noiseless regularity of life; their mutability never hides their sameness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray change as natural and consistent with established character; make growth intelligible as the result of clash with conditions while preserving core identity so readers can extend their lives beyond explicit text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of design and moral/meaning in form
rubrics_metrics.description: The moral or meaning of the book resides in its design; 'without design the scattered scenes will make no picture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that scenes and episodes collocate to form a coherent design; the arrangement of material must announce or reveal the book's purpose, not be a loose accumulation of attractive passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain authorial purpose and avoid vacillation
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer must keep hold of his original reason throughout; vacillation in purpose prevents facts from expressing the intended design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide the book's organizing idea early and sustain it. Shifts in authorial attitude or subject mid-course can dilute thematic force and waste material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid digressions that break the representative function
rubrics_metrics.description: If the novel has a representative or broad theme, individual episodes (e.g., a detailed love-plot) should not 'throw away the value' of a character's representative role by turning them into only a particular heroine of a romance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep subsidiary plots and particulars in service of the larger representational purpose; watch that engrossing subplots do not undermine the book's intended scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and fixity of subject
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel should have 'the subject...absolutely fixed and determined' so the manner of its treatment can be considered with undivided attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the subject precisely (even if treated subtly) before varying method; a stable subject allows critical judgment of technique and prevents wandering composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show rather than merely state — create a single image
rubrics_metrics.description: The book 'is a single image; the facts have no validity in themselves, they are nothing until they have been used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move beyond mere argument or information; arrange facts to produce an artistic impression. Avoid turning a novel into a mere row of facts or a report—craft the presentation so the story 'tells itself' through imagery and dramatic selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate placement of narrative statements (method of stating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different authors choose different ways of placing their statements (e.g., Defoe's directness vs Flaubert's roundabout method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be conscious of where and how information is given — immediate scene, summary, authorial explanation — and choose the method that best serves the book's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate narrator intervention vs showing (use of authorial knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author may intervene to supply past circumstances or interior thought that cannot be perceived by scene alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authorial intrusion judiciously when necessary to provide background or interior perspective; balance 'showing' with occasional necessary telling without breaking the book's overall effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice between scenic and panoramic presentation (point-of-view scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to place the reader before a particular scene ('scenic') or to survey lives from a height ('panoramic').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage alternation between close, particularized scenes and wide, summarizing panoramas; ensure shifts are intentional and readable. Name and control this alternation rather than letting it occur haphazardly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of authorial presence / impersonality
rubrics_metrics.description: Impersonality does not mean absence of judgement; a tactful author dramatizes opinions instead of stating them plainly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control authorial voice: prefer dramatization and embodiment of judgement in characters and events rather than explicit authorial didacticism, while recognizing that the author's view inevitably shapes the representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and consistency of narrative voice / whose eyes we use
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes the author speaks with his own voice, sometimes through a character (e.g., much of Flaubert is in Emma's terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a centre of consciousness or mix voices deliberately. When using a character's viewpoint, render events in terms of that character's standards and perceptions; when using authorial voice, be aware of its evaluative force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial (mood/perception) vs dramatic (objective/stageable) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes can be rendered pictorially (bathed in a character's mood) or dramatically (visible and audible facts that could be staged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether a scene's effect depends on subjective atmosphere or on objective incident; mixing is possible but must be managed. Example: a ball presented through Emma's mood (pictorial) vs a town cattle-show that could be staged (dramatic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve and internal consistency of method (limit latitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist should 'allow himself no more latitude than he requires' and be consistent on some plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gratuitous stylistic shifts; any variety in method should be justified by subject and used sparingly to maintain coherence of tone and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and placement of scenes (earned scenes)
rubrics_metrics.description: A scene must be 'placed...where everything is ready for it'—a scene that is not wanted or fails for lack of preparation is a weakness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scenes are prepared by antecedent material so they achieve their effect. Use summary and chronicle to lead into an occasion that will fulfill and illuminate previous developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of scenes as structural articulation and climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes 'form the articulation of the book' and are the ready means of starting interest and providing climax/resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the novel around scenes that act as pivot points; space summaries and connective material to build toward these climactic scenes so each stage of the story is directed and ripe when reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in treatment of characters across contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must remain 'absolutely true to themselves; wherever we meet them... they are always the people we know.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure character behavior in peace, war, or different settings is consistent with the established inner life; inconsistency should be motivated and intelligible, not accidental or a result of changing authorial method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain centre of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide and sustain 'the centre of vision'—with which character, if any, the reader's primary perception of the story aligns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and hold a centre of vision (or consciously shift it) so the book's focus is clear. The centre affects who interprets events and how scenes are shaded; arbitrary shifting will confuse readers and weaken thematic unity.
